title: Comprehensive Preventive Screening Protocol for Primary Care
implementation_guidance: Implement a systematic approach to preventive screenings based on USPSTF A and B recommendations; screen for anxiety disorders in adults under 65, including pregnant and postpartum persons; screen for anxiety in children and adolescents aged 8-18 years; screen for depression in adults, including pregnant and postpartum persons; screen for major depressive disorder in adolescents aged 12-18; provide low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) after 12 weeks gestation for pregnant persons at high risk for preeclampsia; screen for asymptomatic bacteriuria using urine culture in pregnant persons; assess women with personal or family history of breast, ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer for BRCA testing; offer risk-reducing medications for breast cancer to high-risk women; conduct biennial mammography screening for women aged 40-74; screen for cervical cancer every 3 years with cytology alone for women 21-29, and every 3-5 years with cytology or HPV testing for women 30-65; screen for chlamydia and gonorrhea in sexually active women 24 or younger and older women at increased risk; screen for colorectal cancer in adults aged 45-75 using appropriate modalities.
expected_outcomes: Increased early detection of diseases, reduced morbidity and mortality, improved quality of life, decreased healthcare costs through prevention, enhanced patient engagement in preventive care, reduced disparities in preventive service utilization.
target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals across the lifespan, with particular attention to those with limited access to preventive services, racial and ethnic minorities, and those with social determinants of health barriers.
citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. A and B Recommendations. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation-topics/uspstf-a-and-b-recommendations. Accessed May 29, 2025.
